title: One signer or bookkeeper behind the returns of several unrelated funded organizations
question: Does one person sign, or one outside firm hold the books of, the tax returns of organizations that do not report each other as related?
finding: Across 2,343 returns for tax years ending 2019 or later, 31 names (people and 5 outside firms) sign as officer, are named principal officer, or hold the books for two or more funded organizations that do not report each other as related; 16 do so in the same tax year. Most organizations: Easy Office DBA Jitasa (4).
how: The signing officer, the principal officer and the “books in care of” line of each return were read from the e-file data, never used by the older screens. Organizations tied by Schedule R, or sharing the first two words of their name, count as one.
limits: A finance officer who changes jobs signs for two employers in turn; a shared executive between a district and its foundation is disclosed on both returns; outside bookkeepers serve many small charities. The screen shows where one hand holds several sets of books, which is where the grant-chain and round-trip screens should be read first.
